turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Declan. Form today, yes?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): The knee one, yeah. I've been out there an age and the parking machine ate my change. I'm wrecked.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The nurse called him back, doctor. His blood pressure was through the roof.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the white coat. I'm grand. Can we not make a whole thing of it.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Knee first. Which one?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. It's only a bit sore, for the work form. I'm on my feet the whole shift.
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's been limping on that right knee for months. Don't mind what he tells you.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not limping. There is no limp. It's sore, that's the height of it.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did it start?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, I don't know. Last winter, or the one before. Around then, or after. I couldn't put a date on it.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's three months. He just won't admit it.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): It is not three months. A couple of weeks. Well, actually, maybe a bit over that, no, a couple of weeks. Let me answer.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any swelling?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Locking? Giving way?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Neither.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain at night?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit, if I've stood the shift. Not every night. Um, more after work than in the bed, to be honest.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tablets for it?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol. A gram when it's at me. Not every day.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any other tablets? Blood pressure ones?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing else. I don't take blood pressure tablets.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nurse got 176 over 104.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): White coat. I told her I hate this.
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She did it twice, Declan.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Second reading was 162 over 98. Still high.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): It'll be normal at home. I'm telling you.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Breathless?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Headaches?
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He does. He was on about a headache on Tuesday.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I was not. I don't get headaches. She's mixing me up with herself.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dizzy?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stroke or blood pressure in the family?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had a stroke, years ago. Sure. Can we get to the form, I'm fit to drop.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): When was the pressure last checked, before today?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Haven't a clue. Before Christmas, or the Christmas before. Don't ask me to date it.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): No tablets from me today.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. I wouldn't be taking them.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): This may be white coat hypertension. I'm not calling it that yet. It could still be sustained high blood pressure.
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So what happens now?
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Home readings. Pick up the monitor at reception. Morning and evening for seven days, sitting, five minutes quiet, write every one down.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Seven days. Grand, I suppose.
[SEG0047] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll make sure the mornings get done.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm well able. You don't have to answer for me.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Back in two weeks with the sheet. If the numbers stay up we'll talk tablets then, not before.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll sign the knee form before you go. Light duties, no full shift on your feet. Knee's not hot, and I don't see any swelling now.
